json.name: AICOM (AIMarket)

hlido_opinion.headline: An ambitious self-hosted agent economy — 13 pipeline agents, 17 signed oracles, a federated marketplace — whose most trustworthy feature is that it labels its own cryptography as prototype.
hlido_opinion.body: AICOM proposes a full open economy for autonomous agents: a 13-agent factory that takes a brief through spec, code, QA, security and deploy; a federated hub where shipped capabilities and oracles are signed, indexed and invokable; and pay-per-call settlement over micropayment channels, all self-hosted under MIT/Apache-2.0 with an explicit "no hosted black box — your keys, your data, your host" stance. Seventeen oracles are listed with real mathematical substance (verifiable randomness, optimal transport, persistent homology, graph spectra, Gaussian-process uncertainty), each with Ed25519-signed receipts and optional post-quantum ML-DSA, alongside 377 passing tests. The single most credible thing on the page is the smallest: the Chronos × Platon beacon is labelled "research/prototype crypto honesty", with post-quantum signing off by default. A project that flags its own cryptography as prototype rather than marketing it as quantum-safe is telling you something true, and it is the reason this scores as high as it does. Everything else argues for caution. The scope — factory, marketplace, protocol, oracles, 3D visualisers, Telegram and Discord bots, YouTube release broadcasting, fleet observability — is enormous for what appears to be a very small team, and breadth at that ratio usually means shallow depth somewhere. It is hosted on GitHub Pages, has no adoption evidence, named users, or third-party audit, and "377 tests green" measures self-authored tests, not correctness. Reviewed from the public surface only.

json.tier_rationale: FADING (60) — real technical substance (17 mathematically specified oracles, Ed25519-signed receipts, permissive licensing, genuine self-hosting) and notable intellectual honesty in labelling its own beacon cryptography as research/prototype with post-quantum signing off by default. Held at FADING because the scope is enormous relative to apparent team size, there is no adoption evidence, no third-party audit, and self-authored passing tests are not independent validation of a system that signs and settles value.
what_it_does_well: Labels its own Chronos × Platon beacon as research/prototype cryptography rather than marketing it as production-grade
Post-quantum ML-DSA available but off by default — a conservative, correct default
17 oracles with genuine mathematical specificity, each shipping Ed25519-signed receipts
Fully self-hosted and permissively licensed (MIT/Apache-2.0) — no hosted black box, forkable in every part
Coherent compounding loop: factory ships a capability, hub indexes it, next run discovers and reuses it
Verify step is built into the invocation flow — discover, invoke, verify the signed proof, settle
what_it_fails_at: Scope (factory, marketplace, protocol, oracles, 3D visualisers, bots, broadcasting, observability) is enormous relative to apparent team size
No adoption evidence, named users, or production deployments on the public surface
'377 tests green' counts self-authored tests — not independent validation of a value-signing system
No third-party security audit despite cryptographic signing and on-chain settlement being central
Hosted on GitHub Pages with no institutional footprint or stated continuity commitment
Heavy mythological branding (Dioscuri, Helios, Metis, Gaia, Skopos, Chronos, Platon) obscures rather than explains what each component does
best_for: Researchers and builders exploring self-hosted, non-custodial agent-to-agent economies
Anyone who needs verifiable-math oracles with signed proofs and is able to audit the code themselves
Teams that require full self-hosting and permissive licensing over managed convenience
not_recommended_for: Production systems settling real value — the project labels key cryptography as prototype
Buyers needing an independent security audit before trusting signed receipts
Teams without the capacity to self-host and evaluate a large multi-component stack

red_flags.note: The project self-describes its Chronos × Platon beacon as research/prototype cryptography. This is disclosed honestly and prominently — we flag it so the disclosure is not lost, not because it was hidden.
